avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, controlling emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own resources: park fund money, equipment rental, blue-collar crews. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees distributed across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes toward purchasing trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the Parc Pratt chalet and redeveloping its surroundings, including planting vegetation, partly financed by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, abrasive spreading, parking by-laws.
deneigement.enBref: This year, the Ville and the boroughs hired private companies to handle snow clearing, loading and towing, as well as street and sidewalk cleaning in the spring. Several existing contracts were extended for the 2026-2027 winter and new contracts were awarded for the following seasons. Some boroughs also tightened their rules on contractors who clear snow on private lots.

etapes.texte: Boroughs rented vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives in the spring. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the sidewalk cleaning contract for four private snow removal sectors was awarded to Les Équipements Benco Canada ltée for $271,979.11, taxes included [CA26 27 0034].

Ville-Marie hired companies to handle maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal for Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six public squares including square Dorchester. The borough also extended snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

aSurveiller.texte: The turnkey snow removal contracts awarded for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
Snow removal for roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest runs from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its by-law on snow removal permits is planned for September 8, 2026, with the notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its drinking water and sewer networks, and continuing work sites at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. It is awarding contracts to rehabilitate pipes without trench digging, rebuild pipes and streets, and replace lead service connections. It is also adopting loan by-laws for wastewater disinfection and for new waterworks pipes.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council raises the loan for the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000. The money must be used to complete the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks, and build the oxygen production plant.

etapes.titre: Wastewater treatment plant and new loans
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council awards Construction Deric a $127,984,000 contract to build the oxygen production unit for the disinfection project, and entrusts the monitoring of this work to a group of firms. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector, and the city council begins adopting a $951,000,000 loan for secondary networks.

aSurveiller.texte: The $951,000,000 loan by-law for renewing the secondary waterworks and sewer networks must be adopted on October 19, 2026, according to the timeline in the file.
The rehabilitation of the 600 mm water pipe along Autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp must be completed by December 18, 2026, at the latest.
The shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant is planned for January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
Work on the water pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, must be completed in March 2027.
The work site on rue Guy, between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, is planned to run until December 2027.
The ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant is expected to come into service in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The urban agglomeration council approves construction of a greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then assigns its delivery to the city council, which awards it to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. In July, the borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. a $499,865.92 contract to supply and install two greenhouses.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a $1,091,693.37 contract for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel. The work includes a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture.

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, cycling facilities and plantings.

Two companies are awarded 30-month contracts for general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management of the park. The City also extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor, for $296,349.21 more; the compost is used in particular for park landscaping.

etapes.titre: Snow removal extended by six months
etapes.texte: The City extends by six months the snow removal contract for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the soccer stadium, awarded to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky), for $193,215.49 more.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the Ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and east-west link, closes on November 26, 2026.
Installation work on the greenhouses is to be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The Boisé Ouest sector, 26 hectares, is to be added in 2027 to the 65 hectares already open to the public.
The snow removal extension covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, curb extensions), then from May to August 2028 (final pavement, bike path, plantings).

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, extra mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work was 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, and was to resume on May 15, 2026, to finish on July 10, 2026.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, by adopting conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 summary of the areas listed.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. a contract of $366,117.31, taxes included, to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, for a total expense of $481,850.45. The culvert, damaged by the rains of August 2024, is part of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub modernization project.

The City is entrusting Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée with felling ash trees and other dying trees in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, for $1,370,433.02, taxes included, plus contingencies and quantity variation. The file indicates about 9,000 trees to be felled, from fall 2026 to early summer 2028, to limit the emerald ash borer and secure the sites.

Paysagiste Solarco inc. is awarded snow removal for the service roads and parking lots of the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, for $178,330.82, taxes included, from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028. 9232-3914 Québec inc. is awarded housekeeping maintenance for nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, for a total expense of $704,619.24, from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2030.

aSurveiller.texte: Filing of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance in April 2032.
Start of the snow removal contract on November 1, 2026, until April 30, 2028.
Start of housekeeping maintenance for the nine buildings on November 1, 2026, until October 31, 2030, with an option to extend until October 31, 2031.
Felling work from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres, and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also deploying a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent for the church is estimated at $57,076.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for the winter of 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation, and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and Bain St-Denis setup
etapes.texte: City council adopts a framework to receive private donations for housing, shelter, and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and setup work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract of $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027, and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the litigation over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking its agents' vehicles, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an app.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work involves sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for environmental management of the soil. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, through the environmental liability reserve, to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, then the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for planting sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden land continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for animation activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

The construction work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bulb-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street naming file indicates that site development is planned for around 2032 and that four other public places remain to be named.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collection, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collection in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City extends twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchase and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program lending reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The agglomeration extends the collection contracts for garbage from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from the ecocentres, entrusts two firms with studies on constructions located on former disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program lending dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the dumping authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new district on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply for the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: Extended deadline to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

The City acts as guarantor for a $2,000,000 loan granted by the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on the governance and management of public assets and funds in the district.

The urban agglomeration council adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build main water supply lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella. City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan for soil remediation, sewers and water supply, street redevelopment, and purchases of public domain land.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases at 7301, boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160, rue Namur, including a building housing a municipal sports and recreation centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the sector, and the borough secretary will hold a public consultation meeting.

The City leases parcels of the site to MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, and to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transition nursery. Each lease provides for rent of $100 or $200 before taxes, with the organizations paying for development, maintenance, and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: The City has until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site.
The $128.3M federal grant is conditional on completion of the infrastructure by 2031.
The current leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora), and April 30, 2028 (SOVERDI).

parcs.description: Development and upgrading of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and upgrading of parks in several boroughs: new water play areas, playgrounds, dog parks, sports fields and trails. It is also adjusting several contracts already awarded, notably for contaminated soil. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is having walls and a culvert repaired, submitting an application for a night sky designation, and awarding maintenance contracts.

etapes.texte: The City awards the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It also provides funding to Verdun for environmental and geotechnical studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and the Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec for phase 4 of parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild the culvert under this road, at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and adds the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural environments.

Several contracts already awarded are amended: supervision of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois, work at parc des Hirondelles and parc du Sault-au-Récollet, professional services for parc Percy-Walters and for parc Denise-Morelle, and additional contingencies for parc Villeray.

etapes.titre: New construction projects and land changes
etapes.texte: Contracts are awarded to redevelop parc Denise-Morelle, parc J.O.R.-Leduc and parc Baldwin, and the City pays for the decontamination of parc George-Vernot. It also converts a section of street at parc Campbell Ouest into a local park, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension requests the same change for a 75.2-square-metre laneway strip at parc Le Prévost.

etapes.titre: Maintenance of the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City awards three contracts: snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, the felling of ash trees and declining trees, and janitorial services for nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector.

aSurveiller.texte: Public art competition for parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner selected in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation of the artwork in 2028.
The change of status of a laneway strip at parc Le Prévost must be adopted by the executive committee on October 7, 2026 and by city council on October 19, 2026.
Cap-Saint-Jacques application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.

Grand parc de l'Ouest maintenance contracts: snow removal from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028; janitorial services from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: end of construction in June 2026 and final acceptance of the work in June 2027.
Work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc from August 2026 to June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianizations on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the ordinances that close the streets and authorize terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a piece of land, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee allocates $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058], and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155], and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes a 899-square-metre piece of land at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) status to local park status [CM26 0888], and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes the sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372], and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The ordinance on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie reviews its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough lengthens its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage rate in the sector bounded by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevards Crémazie and Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the City reviewed the plans for view corridors and heights; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work subject to approval in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève indicates it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, police stations, city council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and lending of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the lending of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys 11 patrol motorcycles, extends the janitorial maintenance of the headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It also awards a contract for meals for detained persons and extends maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The City leases 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles. It renews the leases for the training centre in Anjou, police station 15 in Verdun, and police station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights.

The City enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police firearms training, and extends the SPVM mail pickup and delivery service by one year. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in the service's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day at police station 46, on October 23, 2026; the Anjou borough buys 62 tickets.
The port patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered by March 1, 2027 at the latest.
The lease for the metro unit premises of police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, starts on February 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the Société de transport de Montréal's budget and loans, and sells, leases or lends it land to expand its facilities. It also oversees metro construction sites and works with the STM on the extension of the blue line. Borough councils and city council also pass motions on the development of the network.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council approves the STM's 2026 budget and 2026-2035 capital works program, after it was tabled on January 12. It also concludes a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, up to $41,944,604.63 taxes included, plus a contingency budget.

etapes.titre: Metro construction sites and surrounding areas
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville modifies bus waiting stops in its territory as part of the network overhaul, and Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and repair the vault of the green line tunnel 24 hours a day, from June 10 to July 31, 2026. The City signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion at parc Irma-LeVasseur in Outremont, authorizes $250,000 for work related to the Berri-UQAM station construction site, pays $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the UCI Road World Championships, and signs a letter of no objection to the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes spending of $3,808,451.29 taxes included. It then concludes 72-month framework agreements with Artelia Canada and Stantec Experts-conseils for professional services related to the redevelopment of the blue line corridor.

The urban agglomeration approves STM loans and corresponding changes to the 2026-2035 capital works program: start of the replacement of MR-73 train cars, extension of their service life, preferential measures for buses, Réno-Infrastructures phase 4, surface infrastructure repairs, and management of technological and security risks.

City council asks the Québec government to assess options for keeping in Montréal the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line and the project office's expertise. The boroughs of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring public transit projects in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the parking lot south of rue de Louvain starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Repair and expansion work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.

Reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel between Jean-Talon Ouest and Wilderton is planned from June 2026 to March 2028; rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays.
Phase 3 of the work to extend the service life of MR-73 train cars will take place from 2027 to 2031.
The opening of the five new stations of the blue line extension is planned for 2031.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI self-service bike system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike infrastructure projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an ordinance that officially establishes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse, and requires mandatory manoeuvres for drivers up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives to be spread, notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including the repair of the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then retained Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers used as the base for stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and Le Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation for a BIXI station.

City council authorized the submission of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
